=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
  SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
  SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
  SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
  SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
  SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

# Project Kestrel — Buyer review

**Overall recommendation:** Reopen the Seller’s proposed package. Its assertions that the terms are market-standard, agreed at principal level and final are not independently substantiated by the materials provided. The Disclosure Letter identifies risks; it does not, by itself, resolve them. The recommendations below preserve the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free bargain and distinguish confirmed facts from matters still under investigation.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **20% of price: AUD 4.8m**. | A higher cap, initially **100% of price**, with any negotiated reduction limited to general warranties. | **Reopen; negotiate a higher cap.** A AUD 4.8m ceiling may leave the Buyer materially undercompensated for losses. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** each and aggregate **AUD 250,000**; only the excess over the basket is recoverable. | Lower thresholds; related claims aggregated for the de minimis; a **tipping basket** under which the full qualifying amount is recoverable once crossed. | **Replace the excess-only basket and reduce thresholds.** The draft leaves the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty claims must be notified within **18 months after Completion**; limits apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with a workable notice process and sufficient time to investigate and pursue notified claims. | **Extend and confine this limit to general warranties.** Some issues may not emerge within 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties receive the same cap and time limits as general warranties. | A separate fundamental regime, including title and capacity, with a cap of at least **100% of price**, longer survival, and no general de minimis or basket. | **Reject uniform treatment.** Defective ownership or authority can undermine the entire acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Caps, limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to **all claims of any nature**, with no express fraud exception stated. | Express fraud carve-outs from all relevant caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, preserving available remedies. | **Insert a comprehensive fraud carve-out.** No broad limitation should inadvertently restrict recourse for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records, alongside specific disclosures. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope, against the relevant warranty; an agreed, fixed disclosure bundle. | **Reject blanket data-room and public-record disclosure.** Mere availability does not necessarily give the Buyer a meaningful understanding of a risk. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to the Buyer or advisers, including anything **discoverable** in the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; alternatively limit it to actual knowledge of specifically named individuals, without imputed or constructive knowledge and subject to fraud protections. | **Delete or materially narrow.** “Discoverable” shifts diligence risk to the Buyer even where no one identified the issue. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions is included. Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6m, or 30%, of FY26 revenue**. | A completion condition requiring valid written consent **and satisfaction or Buyer-approved waiver of its conditions**, with evidence and no adverse amendment. | **Make effective, unconditional consent a condition to Completion.** A written consent alone may not satisfy the contractual conditions protecting a major revenue stream. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; release to follow Completion. No final discharge is included. | Payoff and release at Completion through the funds flow, with a payoff letter, binding discharge/release undertakings and registration of releases promptly thereafter; debt deducted under the price mechanics. | **Require simultaneous repayment and enforceable release arrangements.** A post-Completion promise alone does not deliver the debt-free/security-free bargain. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | Conditional Completion bonuses total **AUD 420,000** and are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | Identify beneficiaries, vesting conditions and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; allocate the Seller’s economic responsibility and reflect payment or an appropriate price adjustment in the funds flow without double counting. | **Resolve and itemise before signing or Completion.** The liability may crystallise on Completion and reduce the value delivered to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment. DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but is not independent proof of non-payment; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is included. | Verify payment independently; obtain receipt and confirmatory assignment. Broaden the specific indemnity to cover loss arising from defective, challenged or unavailable SOW3 rights, including enforcement and remediation costs. | **Do not treat the payment-only indemnity as adequate.** Payment status and transfer of the project materials remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls it preliminary and unlikely material. A link went to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligations remain unestablished. | Complete investigation promptly, preserve evidence and assess containment, legal notification and remediation with privacy counsel; require information and cooperation, and negotiate a tailored indemnity or other protection informed by findings. | **Investigate and preserve targeted recourse; do not assume a breach or quantified loss.** Potential exposure exists, but the facts are not yet established. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are said to be ordinary-course costs; disclosed materials do not establish whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. | Review each contract, timing and termination right; determine the appropriate debt, working-capital or transaction-expense treatment and avoid double counting. | **Verify before accepting the Seller’s characterisation.** The aggregate amount alone does not establish who should bear the cost. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations and remedies apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A clear claims matrix separating general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax covenant/claims, specific indemnities, price adjustments, debt repayment and fraud, each with expressly tailored limits and survival. | **Draft category-specific rules and precedence.** A general “all Claims” provision could override protections negotiated elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of **100% of issued shares**; Seller relies on it as evidence of title. | Independently check the register and supporting corporate records, capitalisation, transfers, encumbrances and rights to issue or acquire shares; obtain appropriate title warranties and Completion deliverables. | **Verify title and require clean transfer documentation.** The register identifies the recorded holder but does not alone verify every title issue. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP are said to be settled under the general cap and time regime; Ironquay protection is payment-specific. | A separate tax covenant and tax warranty regime with appropriate survival, cap and control provisions; robust IP ownership, assignment and infringement warranties, with tailored protection for identified IP risks. | **Treat both as open and negotiate separately.** General warranty limits may be inadequate for latent tax and core-IP exposure. |

**Additional diligence point:** The disclosed lease material identifies a **notification**, not a landlord-consent requirement, and the Mossvale provision restricts **assignment**, not expressly a share sale. Verify the underlying provisions and comply with any applicable obligations, but do not assume either consent is required on the present record.

*This review is based on the supplied extracts, not the complete SPA, underlying DD documents or independent verification. Proposed thresholds and survival periods are Buyer negotiating positions, not statements of established market practice.*
